content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable way to review AI work and reduce recurring mistakes. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build checkpoints, learning logs, and measurable refinement loops.
actual_capabilities: Defines immediate, interactive, checkpoint, and pattern learning feedback loop types.
Provides templates for baseline metrics, issue logs, learning logs, and quality gates.
Guides self-review using correctness, completeness, quality, security, and clarity checks.
Helps convert recurring issues into prevention strategies for future work.
Structures iterative refinement with checkpoint triggers and measurable improvement metrics.
limitations: It relies on the assistant and user to maintain logs outside the skill text.
It cannot guarantee improvement without clear success metrics and consistent use.
It does not replace tests, code review, or security review.
It may add overhead to small tasks when checkpoints are too frequent.

use_cases.title: Set Team Quality Checkpoints
use_cases.description: Create review points for long coding tasks so issues are found before final delivery.

use_cases.title: Reduce Repeated Writing Issues
use_cases.description: Track recurring clarity or completeness problems and turn them into reusable response checks.

use_cases.title: Measure Assistant Improvement
use_cases.description: Define baseline metrics, compare later results, and record what changed after each iteration.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Feedback Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a simple feedback loop for [task]. Include success metrics and one checkpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Self-Review Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a self-review checklist for [work type]. Cover correctness, completeness, clarity, security, and final verification.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Recurring Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these repeated issues: [list]. Identify patterns, root causes, prevention rules, and measurable follow-up checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Improvement System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a measured improvement system for [team or workflow]. Include baselines, checkpoints, learning logs, and verification metrics.

output_examples.input: I keep missing edge cases in API design reviews.
output: A checkpoint plan before each design decision.
A recurring issue log focused on missing edge cases.
A verification step that checks inputs, errors, and boundary behavior.

output_examples.input: We need better review cycles for long AI coding sessions.
output: Milestone checkpoints after each file or feature section.
Quality gates for requirements, tests, validation, and maintainability.
A final learning log for patterns found during the session.

output_examples.input: Track whether our assistant responses are improving over time.
output: Baseline metrics for accuracy, completeness, clarity, and user edits.
A comparison process for later sessions.
A short record of changes that caused measurable improvement.

best_practices: Define success metrics before starting the loop.
Use checkpoints at natural milestones, not after every small action.
Record recurring issues as prevention rules for future work.
anti_patterns: Adding many checkpoints to small tasks with low risk.
Tracking vague impressions without measurable outcomes.
Treating self-review as a replacement for tests or expert review.

faq.question: What does this skill help improve?
faq.answer: It helps improve response quality through review checkpoints, issue tracking, and measured refinement.

faq.question: Does it store learning across sessions?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and workflows, but storage depends on the assistant environment and user process.

faq.question: Can it replace automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It supports review habits, but tests and expert review remain necessary for high-risk work.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for complex tasks, repeated quality issues, long sessions, or workflows that need measured improvement.

faq.question: What tools does it require?
faq.answer: The skill is mainly instructional and can work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How do I keep the process lightweight?
faq.answer: Use one or two meaningful checkpoints and track only metrics that affect the final result.
